toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.methodChoice: Collected two items: X9 (monthly counts by site with each site's app and coordinator status) to compare sites against each other, then X15 (booking reconciliation from the audit logs and callback notes) to check how the loss happened. Stopped at the 2-item limit.
output.brief:
Mara — it isn't RotaWeave alone, the coordinator cuts alone, the background checks, or Commonplate: the app and the coordinator cuts together caused the fall at Dock Street and Westgate.

The basic RotaWeave plan can't hold a regular's usual weekly slot unless staff book it before Thursday's public release. Staff booked about 74 slots a week at those sites in April; since the coordinators left on 1 May, 3 a week, and an admin seat sits unused. 129 of 213 regulars lost their usual slot; 88% of them have left, against 11% of those who kept it. Millbrook (app, coordinator kept) and Quarry Lane (coordinator gone, no app, paper roster kept by a lead volunteer) are steady. Of 61 lapsed volunteers reached, 44 said nobody booked them; only 2 joined another group. Nearly all had current checks.

Don't cancel RotaWeave ($14,000, lost data, wrong target), suspend checks (required for shifts with children) or purge the roster. Assign someone to book regulars into their usual slots at Dock Street and Westgate, phone the lapsed, review after 60 days, and do the same before Quarry Lane goes live on 6 October. I'm about 85% confident.
